items.note: Story 1: LVCCA organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president (~22 years), creamery 1891.
Story 1: paid by pounds of butterfat not weight; test at own delivery station governs.
Story 1: under payment-by-weight nothing would have cost anyone a cent.

List item with no REQUIRED line, so scored on its core fact: Sill named as Larrow Green buttermaker (Story 2), Teague as bookkeeper (Story 3). Loomis appears only as a source citation, not identified as secretary.
Story 8: Selby is Gideon's son, but manager 'from 1911 or 1913'. Never commits to 1913 (bolded).
Station-gain ledger line not mentioned anywhere in Section A (only in B3/C3/D2/F).
Stories 1-2: Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up-valley, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green.
No account of weighing, composite sample, percent read on the neck after a fixed pipette charge.
Story 2: Ammon & Sons, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897.
Story 2: six dozen pipettes at 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Flat 0.19 in every month not stated in Section A (the flatness appears only in C1b/F).
Only says the error was undetectable by comparing within the lot. Nothing on a pipette being uncheckable without a burette, or on there being none in the county.
Stories 1, 6, 8: Keddie 1861-1934, tester from the first day, twenty-nine seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Test book referenced but its columns, the single hand and the crossed-and-initialed corrections are not described.
Summary leaf's 1896 = 3.80 vs 3.61 from 1898 not given in Section A. 3.61/3.80 appear only as the 1911 interval and the 1958 recorded/true averages.
Story 4: 8 May-10 July 1911, nine weeks, ~3.80 then back, question mark.
Stories 3/8: Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant, the largest patron.

1919 circular present, but the 17 March statement is given only as denying theft plus 'thirty-one times a week'. Missing the 'tested as taught / cannot say why the figures are what they are' element (bolded, required).
Story 8: died 1934 still under the valley's suspicion.
Story 3: the six Hessel Bottom farms, wet hay; Emmet the valley's largest patron.
Brant weigh book's 1 Jan 1897 start and the agreeing scales not in Section A.
Story 3: complaints from 1902 that the milk tested lower than the rest of the valley's. Never conflates the visible gap with 0.19.
Story 3: Grigg committee sampled Jan-Mar 1908 and blamed the land, reported as its theory rather than as fact.
Brant 1910 (200,000 lb at 3.42) and proportional loss not in Section A.
Custody of the weigh book (Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958) absent.
Alder Corners does not appear in any Section A story.
Absent from Section A.
Absent from Section A.
Absent from Section A.
Absent from Section A.
Rosalie Cudd absent from Section A.
Story 5: Merle Strawn, state dairy inspector, Ordell circuit 1907-1936, circuit notebook.
Says he tested for added water with a lactometer, but not that he never found any at Ostrey Hollow.
Story 5: 12 June 1923, against the burette, condemned the lot.
No statement that he wrote no figure and made no report beyond the condemnation.
Story 5: letter 28 June, answer 2 July, new glass in service within the month, 1924 = 3.80 (3.90 rejected), nobody connected it.
Crate's 1923 destination in the loft is only implicit, and the notebooks' route to the college library in 1947 is absent.
Story 6: petition January 1925.
Story 6: Frick's board, 17 March-4 May 1925, one sitting at Ashlin, two in the station weigh room.
Story 6: water, theft, wet hay all heard, 'no cause established'. Proponents named in Story 3.
Four-book exhibit list and Strawn's 1923 notebook as an exhibit absent.
Story 6: dismissed 30 April 1925, no cause established; award 4 May 1925 $3,800 without admission, charged to station account.
One fifth of $19,000 is in Story 7, but the award charged to the account where the 'gain' accumulated since 1898 is not in Section A. Both are required.
Stories 7-8: granddaughter, b. 1931, graduate student in dairy husbandry at Farland, with Professor Leland Vaught.
The assembling of records never before in one room is not stated in Section A.
Story 7: February 1958, loft at Ostrey Hollow, nine survived.
Story 7: 9 March 1958, 16.72 vs marked 17.6, ~95% of the mark (0.88 is implicit).
Stories 2/7: proportional 95%, 3.61 recorded vs 3.80 true, glass 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923.
40M lb, 76,000 lb and $19,000 at 25c are present, but the ledger identity (station-gain total = 76,000) is missing from Section A. All four required.
Bulletin 471, October 1958 is present, but the 35/33/24-year intervals (bolded) are absent.
Granddaughter.
Derivation via Duncan (Ansel's son, Ivy's father), r18. r22's correction noted.
Second cousins, derived via Emmet/Orra siblings -> Roy/Duncan first cousins.
A08 abstained: full vs half sibling cannot be settled, and either way the answer is unchanged.
Gideon Vose, his father.
Significance given as 'insider by birth' plus Teague's claim that Vose knew of the discrepancy from 1916 (an A03 assertion). No Article VII link, no Vose Jerseys.
A01 asserted: 'The sources indicate no real kinship', weighting Duncan's denial.
Asserting either way scores 0. Also never notes that no document names or denies the link.
Adds 0.19 to get a true 3.61 and 380 lb. Key: 3.42/0.95 = 3.60, 7,200 lb, 360 lb owed.
Names both denominators: 76,000/1,444,000 = 5.26% of credited, 76,000/1,520,000 = 5.00% of delivered (headline says '5.25%' but the worked figure is 5.26 on the correct base).
$77.93 summed from the lines.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. short each.
Gives 'about 26 years', not 26 years and 6 weeks (or an exact equivalent). Exact match required. The 25 full years and the reason are correct.
A02 abstained: 1896 intake cannot be determined.
Variable: the measuring instrument, station glass vs borrowed.
Tester, herds, patrons, season, procedure held constant.
~3.61 to ~3.80 for nine weeks, fell back the day the glass returned.
Cause travels with the instrument, not tester/patrons/land. Limits: no size, doesn't identify which measure.
1911 interval (r03/r09/r18), Strawn lactometer (r06), Alder Corners (r10).
Independence argued; Strawn and Alder Corners named as holding without the 1958 measurement.
A09 asserted: 'no', Teague never questioned it, on Kyle's word.
Answers yes, citing the 1919 circular and 1926 address (though grounded mainly in Teague's claim).
Only two of five in B-G: signed the ledger sheets, wrote the 1919 circular. Missing: manager from 1913, argued watering at the 1925 hearing, never names the glassware.
A03 asserted: Vose 'knew about the discrepancy since 1916' treated as established (also in B3).

Row 2 (r15 'whole of 1908' vs Jan-Mar, report vs its own letter) credited. Row 4 resolved to 1913, row 13 to eleven families (both wrong). Row 5 left undetermined. Rows 3, 9 and 11 are handled only in Section A, which is out of scope.
Pairs noticed and broken: NT-16 (eleven, D13 sheet), NT-1 (16.27, measurement sheet + bulletin), NT-11 (12 July, Strawn notebook), NT-9, NT-12, NT-15, NT-17.
A04 only leaned on ('very possibly' reground mold) and never declared unsettleable. A06 not addressed. A10 abstained only in Section A (out of scope for E).
r11 cascade vs its own conclusion, r15 letter vs report, r20 prose vs invoice.
1897 pipettes, 16.72 vs 17.6, 95%, fixed ~5% = ~0.19 off ~3.80, onset spring 1897 and cessation June 1923 with no change on any farm.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer and the 1911 interval.
Theft (Teague) defeated by the ledger showing the cream arriving heavy.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 winter / nothing summer vs a flat 0.19, plus Alder Corners.
A07 asserted: headline verdict 'No' — the board never examined the crate.
A05 abstained: son vs Frick recollections, 'the sources do not let this be settled'.
Summary is ~154 words, over the 150 cap (length violation).
Names ledgers, the inspector's notebook and arguably the 1958 measurement. 'Diaries' and 'family memory' are not keyed series. Fewer than five.
No decoy adopted (hay and water mentioned only as blame), no wrong headline figure.
Has five percent, 1897 and 1958. No 76,000/$19,000, the condemnation is not dated 1923 or called accidental, and neither Keddie is named. 3 of 6, needs 4.

Gullibility A03: Vose knew of the discrepancy from 1916 (D3, B3)
